subproblem.title: Pairing bound for a normalized n-vector: Σ_β w(dx^β)² = 1 implies |w(θ)| ≤ Σ_β |θ(e_β)| (Step 4(b) of the parent proof)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let w ∈ NVector (Eucl P) n be an n-vector on ℝ^P (a continuous linear functional on Covector (Eucl P) n) and let θ ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n be an n-covector. Assume Σ_{β ∈ I(n,P)} w(dx^β)² = 1, where I(n,P) = SimonMultiIndex n P, dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)) and w(dx^β) = euclideanNVectorCoordinate w β. Then |w(θ)| ≤ Σ_{β ∈ I(n,P)} |θ(e_β)|, where θ(e_β) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate θ β = θ(e_{β(0)}, …, e_{β(n−1)}) and e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (w : NVector (Eucl P) n) (θ : Covector (Eucl P) n), ∑ β : SimonMultiIndex n P, (euclideanNVectorCoordinate w β) ^ 2 = 1 → |w θ| ≤ ∑ β : SimonMultiIndex n P, |euclideanCovectorCoordinate θ β|
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 4(b) of the parent proof ("By Step 2 with Q = id, θ_α = Σ_β θ_α(e_β)·dx^β, so ξ(x)(θ_α) = Σ_β θ_α(e_β)·ξ(x)(dx^β) by linearity of ξ(x). At every x with Σ_β ξ(x)(dx^β)² = 1 ... each |ξ(x)(dx^β)| ≤ 1, so |ξ(x)(θ_α)| ≤ c'_α"), stated at a single point. The parent applies it with w := ξ(x) and θ := θ_α at every x where Σ_β ξ(x)(dx^β)² = 1, which holds for μ-a.e. x; this gives |ξ(x)(θ_α)| ≤ c'_α = Σ_β |θ_α(e_β)| for μ-a.e. x.
Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1, θ(e_β) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate θ β = θ(e_{β(0)}, …, e_{β(n−1)}), dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)).

1. Unit coordinates. By definition, euclideanNVectorCoordinate w β = w(dx^β). Fix β ∈ I(n,P). All summands of Σ_γ w(dx^γ)² are squares, hence ≥ 0, so w(dx^β)² ≤ Σ_γ w(dx^γ)² = 1 (Finset.single_le_sum over Finset.univ). Hence |w(dx^β)| ≤ 1, because for real t, t² ≤ 1 iff |t| ≤ 1 (sq_le_one_iff_abs_le_one).
2. Expansion. By the child theorem std_expansion (cmb_covector_eq_sum_coord_smul_wedge, a dependency of this child) applied to θ, θ = Σ_β θ(e_β)·dx^β. This is Step 2 of the parent proof with Q = id.
3. Linearity. w is a linear map on covectors, so applying it to Step 2 (rewrite only the occurrence of θ inside w(θ)) gives w(θ) = Σ_β θ(e_β)·w(dx^β) = Σ_β θ(e_β)·euclideanNVectorCoordinate w β (map_sum, map_smul).
4. Estimate. By the triangle inequality and Step 1, |w(θ)| ≤ Σ_β |θ(e_β)|·|w(dx^β)| ≤ Σ_β |θ(e_β)|·1 = Σ_β |θ(e_β)|, using |θ(e_β)| ≥ 0 (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs, abs_mul, mul_le_of_le_one_right). ∎
If I(n,P) = ∅, the hypothesis reads 0 = 1 and the statement holds vacuously.
proof_key_steps: Each |w(dx^β)| ≤ 1, since w(dx^β)² is one nonnegative summand of a sum equal to 1.
Expand θ = Σ_β θ(e_β)·dx^β (std_expansion) and apply the linear map w: w(θ) = Σ_β θ(e_β)·w(dx^β).

audit.reason: Normalization bounds each vector coordinate by one. Applying the linear functional to std_expansion and estimating the finite sum proves the exact conclusion, including the vacuous empty-index case.
